question.text: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = 8x-y^2-z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,4,1).$
question.explanation:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) = (2,4,1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} ( 8x-y^2-z) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} ( 8x-y^2-z) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} ( 8x-y^2-z) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 8 \ \mathbf i -2y \ \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(2,4,1) &= 8 \ \mathbf i -2(4) \ \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 8 \, \mathbf i -8 \, \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle 8, -8, -1 \rangle \end{align*}

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(2,4,1) \cdot \langle x-2, \: y-4, \: z-1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle 8, -8, -1 \rangle \cdot \langle x-2, \: y-4, \: z-1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] 8(x-2)-8(y-4)-(z-1) & = 0 \\[3pt] 8x -8y - z + 17& = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = e^{y}\cos{2x} + z^2$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},4,1\right).$
question.explanation:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},4,1\right)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} (e^{y}\cos{2x} + z^2) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} ( e^{y}\cos{2x} + z^2) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} ( e^{y}\cos{2x} + z^2) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= -2e^{y}\sin{2x} \ \mathbf i + e^{y}\cos{2x} \ \mathbf j + 2z \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},4,1\right)&= -2e^{4}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \ \mathbf i +e^{4}\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \ \mathbf j + 2(1)\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= -2e^{4} \, \mathbf i + 0 \, \mathbf j +2 \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle -2e^{4}, 0, 2 \rangle \end{align*}

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},4,1\right) \cdot \left \langle x-\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \: y-4, \: z-1 \right \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle -2e^{4}, 0, 2 \rangle \cdot \left \langle x-\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \: y-4, \: z-1 \right \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] %8(x-2)-8(y-4)-(z-1) & = 0 \\[3pt] %8x -8y - z + 17& = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2z + z^2y + y^2x$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
question.explanation:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) = (1,1,-1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} ( x^2z + z^2y + y^2x) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} ( x^2z + z^2y + y^2x) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} ( x^2z + z^2y + y^2x) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= (2xz + y^2) \ \mathbf i + (z^2 +2yx) \ \mathbf j + (x^2 + 2zy)\mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(1,1,-1) &= (2(1)(-1) + 1^2) \ \mathbf i + ((-1)^2 + 2(1)(1)) \ \mathbf j +(1^2 + 2(-1)(1)) \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= -\, \mathbf i + 3 \, \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle -1, 3, -1 \rangle \end{align*}

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(1,1,-1) \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-1, \: z+1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle -1, 3, -1 \rangle \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-1, \: z+1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] -(x-1)+3(y-1)-(z+1) & = 0 \\[3pt] -x + 3y - z - 3& = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = xz^2 + zy^3$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(-2,1,2).$
question.explanation:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) = (-2,1,2)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} ( xz^2 + zy^3) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} ( xz^2 + zy^3) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} ( xz^2 + zy^3) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= z^2 \ \mathbf i + 3zy^2\ \mathbf j + (2xz + y^3)\mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(-2,1,2) &= 2^2 \ \mathbf i +3(2)(1)^2 \ \mathbf j +( 2(-2)(2) + 1^3) \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 4 \, \mathbf i + 6 \, \mathbf j - 7 \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle 4, 6, -7 \rangle \end{align*}

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(-2,1,2) \cdot \langle x+2, \: y-1, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle 4, 6, -7 \rangle \cdot \langle x+2, \: y-1, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] 4(x+2) + 6(y-1)-7(z-2) & = 0 \\[3pt] 4x + 6y - 7z + 16& = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = xe^y-z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,e).$
question.explanation:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) = (1,1,e)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} (xe^y-z) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} (xe^y-z) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} (xe^y-z) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= e^y \ \mathbf i + xe^y \ \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(1,1,e) &= e^1 \ \mathbf i + (1)e^1 \ \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= e \, \mathbf i + e \, \mathbf j - \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle e, e, -1 \rangle \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the surface $\displaystyle 2^{3z^2+2xy} = 2.$ Given that $\mathbf{n} = \langle a,b,c \rangle $ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1, -1, 1),$ what is the value of $\dfrac{c}{b}?$
question.explanation:
Let's define $f(x,y,z) = 2^{3z^2+2xy}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=2.$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1, -1, 1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} \left(2^{3z^2+2xy} \right) \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} \left(2^{3z^2+2xy}\right) \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} \left(2^{3z^2+2xy}\right) \mathbf k\\[5pt] &= \left( 2^{3z^2+2xy}\cdot 2y \ln2 \right) \mathbf i + \left(2^{3z^2+2xy} \cdot 2x \ln2 \right) \mathbf j + \left(2^{3z^2+2xy}\cdot 6z\ln2 \right) \mathbf k\\[5pt] &= 2\ln2\left( y\! \ 2^{3z^2+2xy} \ \mathbf i + x\! \ 2^{3z^2+2xy}\ \mathbf j + 3z\! \ 2^{3z^2+2xy} \ \mathbf k \right) \\[10pt] \nabla f(1, -1, 1) &= 2\ln2\left((-1)\cdot \ 2^{3(1)^2+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)} \ \mathbf i +1\cdot \! \ 2^{3(1)^2+2\cdot 1 \cdot (-1)}\ \mathbf j + 3(1)\cdot 2^{3(1)^2+2\cdot 1\cdot(-1)} \ \mathbf k \right) \\[5pt] &=2\ln2\left( -2^1 \ \mathbf i + 2^1\ \mathbf j + 3 \cdot 2^1 \ \mathbf k \right) \\[5pt] &=4\ln2\left( - \mathbf i + \mathbf j + 3 \ \mathbf k \right) \\[5pt] &= \left\langle -4\ln2,\: 4\ln2, \: 12\ln2 \right\rangle \end{align}

Therefore, our normal vector is $\mathbf{n} = \langle a,b,c \rangle = \left\langle -4\ln2,\: 4\ln2, \: 12\ln2 \right\rangle.$

Finally, $\require{cancel}\dfrac{c}{b} = \dfrac{12\ln2}{4\ln2}=3.$

question.text: Consider the surface $z^2x^2 =xy.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,4,2).$
question.explanation:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

\begin{align*} z^2x^2 &= xy \\[3pt] z^2x^2 - xy &= 0 \end{align*}

If we set $f(x,y,z) = z^2x^2 - xy$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,4,2)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} (z^2x^2 - xy) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} (z^2x^2 - xy) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} (z^2x^2 - xy) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= (2xz^2-y) \ \mathbf i - x \ \mathbf j + 2x^2z \ \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(1,4,2) &= (2(1)(2)^2-4) \ \mathbf i - (1) \ \mathbf j + 2(1)^2(2) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 4 \, \mathbf i - \mathbf j + 4 \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle 4, -1, 4 \rangle \end{align*}

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(1,4,2) \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-4, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle 4, -1, 4 \rangle \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-4, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] 4(x-1)-(y-4)+4(z-2) & = 0 \\[3pt] 4x - y + 4z - 8 & = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the surface $z\cos(x+y) - xyz= 2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}2.$ Given that $\mathbf{n} = \langle a,b,c \rangle $ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $\left( \dfrac{\pi}{2}, -\dfrac{\pi}{2}, 2\right),$ what is the value of $\dfrac{a}{b}?$
question.explanation:
Let's define $f(x,y,z) = z\cos(x+y) - xyz.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}2.$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $\left( \dfrac{\pi}{2}, -\dfrac{\pi}{2}, 2\right)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} \left(z\cos(x+y) - xyz \right) \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} \left(z\cos(x+y) - xyz \right) \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} \left( z\cos(x+y) - xyz \right) \mathbf k\\[5pt] &= \left(-z\sin(x+y) -yz \right) \mathbf i + \left( -z\sin(x+y) -xz \right) \mathbf j + \left( \cos(x+y) - xy\right) \mathbf k\\[10pt] \nabla f\left( \dfrac{\pi}{2}, -\dfrac{\pi}{2}, 2\right) &=\left(-2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)\ \mathbf i + \left(-2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right) \ \mathbf j + \left(\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \pi \ \mathbf i - \pi \ \mathbf j + \left(1+ \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}\right) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \left\langle \pi,\: -\pi , \: 1+\dfrac {\pi^2}{4} \right\rangle \end{align}

Therefore, our normal vector is $\mathbf{n} = \langle a,b,c \rangle = \left\langle \pi,\: -\pi ,\: \dfrac {\pi^2+4}{4} \right\rangle.$

Finally, $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{\pi}{-\pi}=-1.$

question.text: Consider the surface $z^2y +16= 4\sqrt{x} + y.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(4, -1,3).$
question.explanation:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

\begin{align*} z^2y +16&= 4\sqrt{x} + y. \\[3pt] z^2y - 4\sqrt{x} - y&= -16 \end{align*}

If we set $f(x,y,z) =z^2y - 4\sqrt{x} - y$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-16.$

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(4,-1,3)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} (z^2y - 4\sqrt{x} - y) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} (z^2y - 4\sqrt{x} - y) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} (z^2y - 4\sqrt{x} - y) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \ \mathbf i +(z^2-1) \ \mathbf j + 2zy\ \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(4,-1,3) &= -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4}} \ \mathbf i + (3^2 -1) \ \mathbf j + 2(3)(-1) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= - \, \mathbf i + 8\ \mathbf j - 6 \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle -1, 8, -6 \rangle \end{align*}

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(4,-1,3) \cdot \langle x-4, \: y+1, \: z-3 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle -1, 8, -6 \rangle \cdot \langle x-4, \: y+1, \: z-3 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] -(x-4)+ 8(y+1) -6(z-3) & = 0 \\[3pt] - x + 8y - 6z + 30 & = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the surface $xy^2 + 6= zx^2.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-2,-1,1).$
question.explanation:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

\begin{align*} xy^2 +6 &= zx^2 \\[3pt] xy^2 - zx^2 &= -6 \end{align*}

If we set $f(x,y,z) = xy^2 - zx^2$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-6.$

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

\[ \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle = 0. \]

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-2,-1,1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \nabla\! f(x,y,z) &= f_x(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{i} + f_y(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{j} + f_z(x,y,z) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} (xy^2 - zx^2) \ \mathbf i + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y} (xy^2 - zx^2) \ \mathbf j + \dfrac {\partial}{\partial z} (xy^2 - zx^2) \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= (y^2 - 2xz) \ \mathbf i + 2xy \ \mathbf j - x^2 \ \mathbf k \\[10pt] \nabla\! f(-2,-1,1) &= ((-1)^2 - 2(-2)(1)) \ \mathbf i + 2(-2)(-1) \ \mathbf j - (-2)^2 \ \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 5 \, \mathbf i + 4\mathbf j - 4 \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \langle 5, 4, -4 \rangle \end{align*}

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

\begin{align*} \nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \nabla f(-2,-1,1) \cdot \langle x+2, \: y+1, \: z-1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] \langle 5, 4, -4 \rangle \cdot \langle x+2, \: y+1, \: z-1 \rangle & = 0 \\[3pt] 5(x+2)+ 4(y+1)-4(z-1) & = 0 \\[3pt] 5x + 4y - 4z + 18 & = 0 \end{align*}
